author: NorthEast News Desk
body: New Hampshire Humanities has received $25,000 to support its Connections reading program, which works with people in substance-use treatment, correctional settings and other community programs. NHPR reported that the award combines support from Granite United Way’s Opioid Abatement Community Grants Program and the New Hampshire Charitable Foundation’s Alice Hale Penniman Memorial Fund.

Connections organizes guided book discussions and gives participants as many as four books that they can keep or share with children and other relatives. More than 600 people have participated, according to the program. Its partnerships also extend to adult-education centers and organizations serving new Americans and people with disabilities.

Program leaders said the grant will help protect direct services after the loss of federal funding reduced the operating budget by 25% last year. The money is intended for programming so host organizations and participants do not absorb that gap.

The model uses literature as a practical tool for connection during treatment and major life transitions. Organizers are also seeking discussion leaders who understand the communities being served, allowing the reading selections and conversations to reflect a wider range of experiences across New Hampshire.
dek: The Connections program will use the funding to keep books and guided discussions available through treatment, correctional and community partners.
headline: New Hampshire literature program receives $25,000 recovery-services grant
